summary: This Dockerfile creates a Docker image based on Ubuntu and installs Google Chrome in it. It sets up a non-interactive environment to avoid prompts during installation, downloads Chrome, installs it, and cleans up temporary files to keep the image smaller. When the container runs, it launches Chrome with flags that disable some features for better compatibility in containerized environments.

explanations.3: This tells the system not to prompt for user input during installation — it just proceeds with defaults, which is necessary in automated container builds.
explanations.6: The backslash at the end of this line continues the command on the next line, so all these apt-get commands run as one chain rather than separate steps.
explanations.9: After installing Chrome, this removes the package manager's cache files that are no longer needed, reducing the final image size.
